messages:
Aisha Khan: quick follow-up from the RFC: proposing a 'local-sentinel' pattern where edge routers make trusted, short-lived routing verdicts (throttle / divert / cut) based on local health signals. central control only publishes signed policy snapshots. initial idea, high level. thoughts?
Tom Becker: signed snapshots sounds good to avoid rogue routers. what counts as a health signal? latency spikes, model error rate, kv miss flood?
Aisha Khan: yep. we plan to use three micro-signals: latency_p95 deviation, token_error_rate, and inflight_queue_depth. we combine into a single health_score.
Nina Shah: curious about divergence: if routers act locally for safety, how do we prevent a tenant split where some routers sever traffic and others don't?
Aisha Khan: local verdicts are stamped with policy_version + signature + lease_ttl. routers must advertise active verdicts to the control plane; control plane can revoke or supersede by publishing a new signed snapshot with higher epoch. leases are short (e.g., 10s) to avoid long-lived splits.
Rajesh Menon: what about global overrides for legal/compliance reasons? must be immediate. signing helps but how do we ensure immediate acceptance?
Aisha Khan: central snapshots include an "enforce_immediate" flag. when set, routers bypass lease wait and apply the new snapshot instantly. otherwise they respect in-flight grace.
Tom Becker: can we get a minimal snapshot example inline?
Aisha Khan: sure:
```
{
  "epoch": "2024-05-01T12:00:00Z",
  "policy_id": "canary-v3",
  "enforce_immediate": false,
  "rules": [
    {"signal":"health_score", "cut_threshold": 0.35, "divert_pct": 20},
    {"signal":"token_error_rate", "cut_threshold": 0.02}
  ],
  "lease_ttl_s": 10
}
```
Nina Shah: okay. another ops concern: cache/keyspace churn if we divert to older variant. we saw past incidents with cold storms.
Rajesh Menon: suggestion: when a router issues a cut to fallback, it also emits a shadowing request to the fallback variant for a small fraction to keep caches warm. call it 'warm-shadow'.
sre-bot: note: warm-shadow increases qps on fallback, might affect billing/rate limits.
Tom Becker: subtle thought: verdict provenance must be queryable in traces and metrics. add decision_id and reason tags on request spans so postmortem can reconstruct why traffic moved.
Aisha Khan: agreed. we'll attach decision_id and verdict_reason (probe / policy / override). also emit an aggregate stream of local-decisions to the telemetry bus for cross-router reconciliation.
Nina Shah: rollout controls: tenants want custom risk budgets. can we have per-tenant safety_budget and min_live_pct to avoid full cut by a single node?
Aisha Khan: yes, snapshot supports tenant overrides. default global budget is soft; tenant override is prioritized in merging. min_live_pct included.
Rajesh Menon: rejoin/backoff strategy? avoid flapping. propose exponential backoff with jitter + a linear cool-down window.
Tom Becker: also track 'recovery_confidence' using a short probe window before rejoining 100%. e.g., watch 30s of stable probes.
Aisha Khan: good. we'll add recovery_confidence_window_s.
sre-bot: reminder: need a runbook mapping sentinel states to ops playbooks (alert thresholds, who to page).
Nina Shah: will coordinate with eng-sre on that.
Tom Becker: last: network partition case. if router loses control plane connectivity, it must still honor signed snapshot until lease expiry, then transition to a safe default (divert to fallback) rather than open the path.
Aisha Khan: absolutely. default safe=divert. ok squad, I'll put a draft PR for the snapshot format + telemetry hooks and a short design doc for the runbook. thanks all :white_check_mark:
